name: InterContinental Melbourne The Rialto
positioning: Heritage hotel on Collins Street in central Melbourne, set in 1890s neo-Gothic buildings joined by a glass atrium
best_for: Travelers who want a central Collins Street base for Melbourne's laneways, galleries and stadiums
Guests drawn to heritage architecture with contemporary interiors

facts.text: The hotel is on Collins Street in the heart of Melbourne.
The glass atrium, ornate windows and original brickwork showcase 1890s neo-Gothic architecture.
The building is on the National Heritage List.
The heated indoor pool and hot tub overlook the Melbourne skyline.
The pool and hot tub are complemented by a Scandinavian-inspired sauna and a light-filled fitness centre.
Some suites may include a Collins Street view and a separate jetted bath with walk-in rain shower.
Alluvial Restaurant serves seasonal dining beneath the hotel's atrium.
Bluestone Wine Lounge features fine wines from Victoria and Australia.
The location gives access to Melbourne's laneways and luxury boutiques, the National Gallery of Victoria, the MCG and Marvel Stadium.
The concierge can procure tickets to Arts Centre Melbourne and arrange a backstage tour.

highlights.text: The hotel is two buildings, the older Gothic Rialto and the Romanesque Winfield Building, linked by a soaring glass ceiling over what was once a wide lane.
The atrium is a spectacle of light, angles, marble, mosaic, bluestone and carefully selected local art.
The rooftop pool has floor-to-ceiling windows with views over the CBD and out to the bay.
The club lounge offers daily breakfast, afternoon tea, evening canapés and all-day refreshments.
The Signature Suites offer expansive living spaces and bespoke furnishings.

considerations.text: Pets are not allowed at the hotel.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing typical of luxury heritage hotels in prime CBD locations.
